name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills district, a colonial hill station at about 1,500 m elevation known for pine forests, lakes, markets, and as the base for exploring Khasi Hills attractions. Features a blend of Khasi culture and British-era architecture.
facts: Headquarters of East Khasi Hills and state capital
Known as the Scotland of the East
Base for day trips to Sohra, Mawlynnong and other sites

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at about 1,965 m, located roughly 10 km from Shillong. Offers panoramic views of the city, surrounding hills, and distant Bangladesh plains; popular for sunrise and sunset photography.
facts: About 10 km from Shillong city centre
Sacred site for local Khasi with seasonal rituals
Popular evening hangout for city lights views

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall near Shillong, named for a rock formation resembling an elephant's head. Cascades through dense forest; accessible with viewing platforms and a short walk.
facts: Named after elephant-shaped rock (now less distinct)

name: Ward's Lake
description: Man-made lake in the heart of Shillong, also called Nan Polok. Surrounded by flower gardens, wooden bridges, and a boathouse; a popular recreational spot named after a former British official.
facts: Also known as Nan Polok in Khasi

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures (Museum)
description: Museum in Shillong showcasing the cultures, lifestyles, and artifacts of indigenous peoples of Northeast India. Features traditional huts, tools, and exhibits on tribal heritage.

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Historic town in East Khasi Hills, once recorded as the wettest place on Earth. Gateway to numerous waterfalls, caves, living root bridges, and dramatic escarpment views toward the Bangladesh plains.
facts: Local name Sohra; formerly world's wettest place
Base for Nohkalikai, root bridges and caves

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at 340 m (1,115 ft), cascading from the Sohra plateau into a turquoise pool. Named after a local legend; dramatic cliff views amid one of the wettest regions.
facts: Height 340 metres, tallest plunge in India

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Segmented seven-stream waterfall plunging about 315 m over limestone cliffs near Mawsmai. Also known as Seven Sisters Falls; spectacular during monsoon with views toward the plains.

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone cave near Sohra with illuminated pathways, stalactites, and short walkable route suitable for beginners. One of the most visited caves in Meghalaya.

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, formed by guiding Ficus elastica roots over generations. Requires a steep trek of ~3,500 steps from Tyrna; unique bioengineering and swimming pools nearby.

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Known as Asia's cleanest village, a model of community-driven cleanliness with bamboo pathways, orchids, and skywalk views toward Bangladesh. Features living root bridges nearby and matrilineal Khasi culture.
facts: About 90 km from Shillong near Bangladesh border
Skywalk and nearby Riwai root bridge

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon and viewpoint near Smit, offering sweeping views of deep valleys, ridges, and clouds below. Often called the Grand Canyon of Meghalaya; accessible for short walks and photography.

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest (Law Lyngdoh)
description: Ancient sacred grove protected by Khasi tradition for centuries; dense primary forest with monoliths, biodiversity, and strict rule against removing anything. One of the best-preserved law kyntang in Meghalaya.
facts: No removal of plants or objects allowed
Home to rare flora and monolith sites

name: Arwah Cave
description: Limestone cave near Sohra featuring fossilized marine remains, large chambers, and accessible lit pathways. Less crowded alternative to Mawsmai with unique geological interest.

name: Kongthong Village (Whistling Village)
description: Unique Khasi village where residents communicate using individual whistled tunes (Jingrwai Lawbei) composed by mothers at birth. Offers living root bridges, eco-huts, and cultural immersion; UNWTO recognized.
